name: Pop Art
visualIdentity: Supplemental reference, not a direct source-collection label. Mass-culture objects, comic imagery, repeated panels, bold color fields, heavy outlines, and optional halftones create a graphic look. Lettering is part of the composition; repetition, color swaps, scale changes, and split screens support one clear focal image. Comic imagery or halftones alone do not establish Pop Art.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to single iconic images. Inferred suitability: product promos, campaign headlines, event teasers, music promos, social loops, explanatory or editorial stories, and concise interactive presentations when a focal image and clear narrative or selection structure help. For interactive HTML, scroll chapters, storytelling, or a horizontal card track can organize content when they suit the material.
limitations: Keep one focal image per frame and enough time to read. Avoid thin type, halftones over letterforms, too many simultaneous words, red small text, strobe-like full-panel swaps, random colors, and transitions that hide causality or essential copy. Omit chapter or carousel patterns when there is no meaningful progression, cards need simultaneous comparison or long reading, or clipping obscures context. Do not imply autoplay, wrapping, or continuous-shot cuts by default.
palette: Optional new-artwork suggestion: background #FFF6D6, foreground/ink #171717, accents #E8393E, #F1C932, #2671C6; five discrete colors, no gradients. These are not canonical: preserve task, brand, reference, semantic-role, and asset colors exactly. Keep the style's color families and limits; layout roles do not authorize recoloring. Red is decorative only for small text; dark text on red misses the normal-text target. Suggested readable pairs include dark on background or yellow and background on blue. Recheck actual compositing; contrast ratios alone do not guarantee readability.
motionAndInteraction: Use authored repetition, color substitution, scale changes, split screens, staggered panel changes, and deliberate reading holds. Preserve sharp cuts and impacts where intended; do not add generic bounce or smoothing. Optional transitions coordinate outgoing/incoming chapters through one bounded, reversible progress state; interactive HTML may map finite scroll to that state, while video uses timed scenes. Optional card tracks use bounded horizontal offsets and explicit snap selection, with accessible buttons/keyboard as well as swipe. Interactive storytelling may map scroll to ordered states and return coherently on backward scroll. Video must derive all states from seekable composition time, independent of live input; direct and reverse seeks must render deterministically. Reduced-motion/static states are appropriate for HTML.
audio: No fixed genre, tempo, voice, or required audio layer is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied choices and assets. Suggest scene-level changes that support the motion and preserve speech and reading comprehension. Do not assume assets exist or default silently to instrumental music. Synchronize, mix, and check intelligibility, balance, clipping, and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Prepare color separations, comic contours, and repeated panels. Stable halftones may be drawn in Canvas; keep SVG or HTML lettering crisp. SVG suits scalable shapes, strokes, masks, and clipping; Canvas suits deterministic textures and bitmaps. A custom luminance halftone shader is optional, maps darker tones to larger dots on an angled grid, and requires alias/flicker and gamma checks. Protect text and emissive screens with masks. Load fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache stateful effects. Do not treat optional libraries or supplied example assets as mandatory.
combinations: Alone suits a single iconic image. Kinetic typography (style-093) can add outlined, timed headlines around one focal image; keep lettering outlined in #171717 and red away from small text. Beat-timed repetition/color substitution (style-105) suits music promos or loops: stagger panel changes, keep halftone fixed, use palette tokens only, and avoid full-frame strobe. Chapter, carousel, and storytelling patterns are optional; select only when scene geometry and narrative support them.
productionApproach: Style renderer owns drawing, separations, contours, panels, type, and halftones; motion engine owns trajectories and transitions, with one owner per animated property. SVG/Canvas are native options; GSAP is the primary seekable motion route, while Motion or mo.js are optional only with explicit deterministic synchronization. HyperFrames is the default composition/export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, and record why. Pipeline handles timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export, not style construction. Inspect representative frames and full output for legibility, color, stability, timing, and sync.
